author: 滇西小哥 Dianxi Xiaoge
description:
※Click "cc" on the lower right menu to choose your subtitle language.

Stinky ginseng grows in the red soil of Yunnan’s high mountains and ripens every winter. When freshly dug up, its thick root releases a pungent, almost unbearable juice — truly hard to smell.
But after long, slow simmering, that sharp odor transforms completely. It melts into the broth, turning into a deep, herbal fragrance, much like danggui (angelica root) and astragalus, and brings a uniquely rich, sweet taste that’s so good it can make your eyebrows jump.
Among local people, stinky ginseng is considered just as nourishing as real ginseng. Every winter, families make sure to enjoy it a few times. A bowl of stinky ginseng chicken soup warms the body from the inside out.
The only side effect?
The next day comes with some impressively loud and endless farts — as if all the stale energy inside the body has been flushed out for good.
